title: MAY 0 1977 (76-608)
text:
MAY 0 1977
76-608 : Fish and Wildlife Service
FRANK AND RENE LOCK : Special Use Permit
: Appeal Dismissed
By letter dated January the Acting Regional Director,
Fish and Wildlife Service Department of the Interior, Denver,
Colorado, informed Frank Lock, appellant herein, that a special use
permit for grazing on the UL Bend-Bowdoin National Wildlife Refuge
would not be issued to him for calendar year 1976. The denial was
based on alleged permit violations which had occurred in previous
years. The original notification was returned unclaimed, but a sub
sequent notification by date of February 18, 1976, was received by
appellant Rene Lock, though the actual date of receipt is in
controversy.
The letter of January 9 declared that "Title 50, Code of Fed
eral Regulations, Section 29.22, makes reference to appeal proce
dures which are available should you desire to pursue an appeal."
By letter dated march 22, appellants filed a notice of appeal
from the decision of the Acting Regional Director.
On April 21, 1976, appellants filed a statement of reasons in
support of the appeal with this Board and requested that the board
refer the case to the Hearings Division for the assignment of an
administrative law judge who would hold a fact-finding hearing.
See 43 CFR 4.41b.
In a submission of 14, 1976, the Office of the Field
Solicitor moved that the Board dismiss the appeal of Frank and
Rene Lock on the ground, inter that the appeal was not prop
erly before the Board. Inasmuch as we believe that there is merit
to the position of the Solicitor, we hereby grant the motion and
dismiss the appeal.
The regulation cited by the Acting Regional Director in his
letter of January 9, 50 CFR 29.22, states, in relevant part:

76-608
An appeal may be taken from any final disposition
of the Regional Director, to the Director, U.S. Fish
and Wildlife Service, and, from the latter's decision
to the Secretary of the Interior. Such appeals may
be taken pursuant to 43 CFR Parts 1840 and 1850 except
that (a) a ll references to the "Director" or "Director,
Bureau of Land Management," are changed to Director,
U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service The above proce
dures for hearing and appeals, 30 provided and amended,
are hereby adopted as procedures for hearings and
appeals by said U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service.
This regulation was originally promulgated as proposed rule
making on June 20, 1969, 34 FR 9680, and was adopted on December 19,
1969, 34 FR 19907. Parts 1840 and 1850 of 43 CFR at that time pro
vided detailed regulations governing the taking of appeals from
decisions officers of the Bureau of Land Management and proce
dures to be utilized in hearings arising out of such appeals.
Under the procedures then in force, appeals from adverse decisions
by officials were first taken to the Director, BLM, where they
were processed by the Office of Appeals and Hearings. Appeals from
decisions of the Office of Appeals and Hearings could then be taken
to the Secretary. Appeals to the Secretary were normally decided
by the Assistant Solicitor for Public Lands.
Motivated in part by a concern that the appellate procedure
raised questions concerning a combination of functions within the
Office of the Solicitor, the Department, effective July 1,
established the Office of Hearings and Appeals consisting of the
Director and various Boards of Appeal. 35 FR 10012 (June 18,
1970). Parts 1840 and 1850 were amended to reflect these changes.
Part 1840 now reads, in relevant part: "For special procedural
rules applicable to appeals from decisions of Bureau of Land
Management officers or of law judges, within the
jurisdiction of the Board of Land Appeals, Office of Hearings
and Appeals, see Subpart E of Part 4 of this title. * *
43 CFR 1840.1." The hearing regulations, 43 CFR 1850, were
similarly changed.
With exceptions, the regulation now in effect establishes
a procedure in which persons appealing from a decision of the
Regional Director must first appeal to the Director. Appeals
taken from adverse decisions of the Director are then properly
considered by the Office of Hearings and Appeals. Thus, the
procedure is parallel to the procedure utilized to obtain review
of decisions of the Conservation Division, Geological Survey,
as well as the Bureau of Indian Affairs in matters concerning
mineral permits and leases. See 30 CFR 290 and 30 CFR 221.66,
250.81.

Unfortunately, the subject matter of the instant case falls
within the exceptions. Regulation 50 CFR 29.22 does not, by its
terms, apply herein. That regulation is found in subpart B of
Part 29, which only applies to rights-of-way. the proposed
rulemaking published on June 20, 1969, listed the change under the
heading "Rights-of-way Regulations." Moreover, nothing
50 CFR 29.22 lends itself to an interpretation that it was to
apply to other subparts within Part 29. For example, "Regional
Directors" is not defined in either subpart A or C of Part 29, nor
is the position even mentioned in these two subparts. All refer
ences to the Regional Director occur only in subpart B. Yet, a
reading of 50 CFR 29.22 makes it clear that the decisions which
are subject to an appeal to the Director, are those of the
Regional Director. We are forced to hold, therefore, that nothing
in 50 CFR 29.22 grants this Board jurisdiction over the instant
Nor can we find any other source by which this Board would
acquire jurisdiction over the instant appeal. While 43 CFR 4.1(3)
provides a very general grant of authority to the Board to decide
"finally for the Department appeals to the head of the Department
from decisions rendered by officials relating to the
use and disposition of public lands their resources," the terms
of 43 CFR limit the grant of the right to appeal to persons
adversely affected "by a decision of an officer of the Bureau of
Land or of an administrative law judge." Thus, absent
a specific grant of a right to appeal, such as is provided in
30 CFR 290 and 50 CFR 29.22, persons adversely affected by deci
sions of departmental officials other than those in the Bureau
of Land Management cannot seek review of the adverse decision
before this Board. The appeal, therefore, must be dismissed.
Accordingly, pursuant to the authority delegated to the Board
of Land Appeals by the Secretary of the 43 CFR 4.1, the
appeal is dismissed.
/s/ Newton
Newton Frishberg
Chief Judge
We concur:
Stuebing S/ Douglas E.
Edward W. Stuebing Douglas E. Henriques
Administrative Judge Judge
